candidate.answerReason: The product of the first n terms is 10 raised to n(n+1)/22. At n=10 it equals 100,000; at n=11 it exceeds that value, and the products increase with n.

methods.label: Add the exponents in the product
methods.explanation:
Multiplying powers with the same positive base adds their exponents. Thus, for a positive integer \(n\), the product \(P_n\) of the first \(n\) terms is
\[
P_n=10^{(1+2+\cdots+n)/11}
=10^{n(n+1)/22},
\]
using the arithmetic-sum formula \(1+2+\cdots+n=n(n+1)/2\).

Every sequence term is greater than \(1\), so adding another factor strictly increases the product. At \(n=10\),
\[
P_{10}=10^{110/22}=10^5=100{,}000.
\]
Equality is insufficient because the question says “exceeds.” The next value gives
\[
P_{11}=10^{132/22}=10^6>100{,}000.
\]
All products with fewer than ten factors are smaller than \(P_{10}\), so the smallest possible \(n\) is \(\boxed{11}\), choice E.
methods.levelReason: Positive-base exponent laws, an arithmetic sum, and comparison of consecutive integer cases are within high-school precalculus.
